newsitem.title: UK: MAJOR ANNOUNCES SPORTING AMBASSADORS FOR SCHOOLS.
newsitem.headline: MAJOR ANNOUNCES SPORTING AMBASSADORS FOR SCHOOLS.

text.p: John Major, Britain's sports-loving prime minister, announced on Friday he would send "ambassadors" into schools in an attempt to inspire more youngsters to take up sport.

Former English cricket captain Sir Colin Cowdrey would head the Sports Ambassadors' Committee, Major told members of his Conservative party at their annual conference. The committee will be asked to produce clear proposals by the end of the year.

"I'm going to set up a team of sporting ambassadors -- widely drawn from the best role models in sports, our leading athletes, past and present -- who'll visit schools and talk to pupils, teaching staff, school governors and parents, to enthuse and inspire and encourage," Major said.
British sports fans were disappointed by their athletes winning just one gold at the Atlanta Olympics.
Sports officials put part of the blame on the government's lack of funding for sport. Others said the reduction in sport played at school was partly to blame.
"I want them (children) to enjoy sport and they'll enjoy it more if they play to win. Take it from me -- winning is fun," Major said.
